recipes.name: Asian Glazed Chicken Thighs
ingredients_raw: 0.33333334326744 cup soy sauce (such as Silver Swan®)

steps.text: Whisk vinegar, soy sauce, honey, toasted sesame oil, chili garlic sauce, minced garlic, and salt together in a bowl. Pour 1/2 of the marinade into a resealable plastic bag; retain the other 1/2 of the marinade for the sauce. Place chicken thighs into the bag, coat with the marinade, squeeze out excess air, and seal the bag. Marinate in the refrigerator for 1 hour, turning the bag once or twice.

Preheat the oven to 425 degrees F (220 degrees C). Meanwhile, pour reserved marinade into a saucepan over medium heat. Bring to a boil and simmer, stirring often, until thick, 3 to 5 minutes; set sauce aside.
Remove chicken thighs from the marinade and shake off excess. Discard used marinade. Place chicken thighs into a 9x13-inch baking dish; brush with 1/3 of the thickened marinade from the saucepan.

Bake in the preheated oven for 30 minutes, basting one more time after 10 minutes; an instant-read thermometer inserted into a chicken thigh should read 165 degrees F (75 degrees C). Let stand for 5 or 10 minutes.
Bring sauce back to a boil for 1 minute; serve over chicken and sprinkle with green onions.

raw_recipe.headline: Asian Glazed Chicken Thighs
raw_recipe.description: These baked Asian chicken thighs are deliciously spicy, sticky, and garlicky thanks to the addition of chili sauce, honey, and fresh garlic.

video.description: In this video, we'll show you how to marinate and bake these Asian-inspired chicken thighs. First we whisk up a rice vinegar, sesame, soy sauce, and chili-garlic marinade for the chicken. After an hour we'll bake and baste the thighs with the remaining sauce until nicely glazed. Serve this up with steamed rice, seared snap peas, and toasted sesame seeds for a perfect weeknight dinner.

review.reviewBody: My husband -- who hates chicken with an unnatural passion the likes of which one only expects to encounter in relation to the usual suspects: anchovies, liver, random Kardashians, and the like -- THAT guy had this to say of this recipe: "Wow. That's good chicken. And you know it pains me to say that." And THEN, my 11 y.o. kid ate an unprecedented THREE servings of a non-dessert-related dish. It was like I won the Mom Olympics tonight. Got recruited on the Chinese team and plain won that thing. Many thanks for the recipe. I didn't have the fancy Chinese chili, so I used run-of-the-mill chili powder. Also, I put a broil on the last few minutes to give it a bit of edge. Apparently, it was all magic.

This is my new go-to meal to cook when I am delivering a meal to someone else. I make it with brown rice (throw in a couple of chicken bouillon cubes with the rice water and finish with fresh parsley. I use chicken thigh fillets--skinless and boneless. I also have made this so often that I don't waste the precious sauce by marinating the meat at all! I baste the meat a few times and save the yummy asian sauce to drizzle over the rice. This is seriously the best chicken recipe I've ever made! Enjoy!

We enjoyed this sauce very much. Very tasty. My husband is Asian so I increased the chili sauce. Next time I make it, I'm going to increase the recipe for the sauce. As it is, it is just enough but I like a little extra.
this was good, but i thought it needed something...maybe fresh ginger in the sauce/marinade or toasted sesame seeds or chopped peanuts sprinkled on top for crunch...

It was really good! I made it for my husband's birthday. I doubled the recipe and added some ginger and used the S&B Crunchy garlic with chili oil instead of the chili garlic sauce because it's not in stores right now. I also put the chicken on a rack in the pan so they wouldn't stew in the drippings. I served it with steamed rice and stir fried vegetables. I poured the extra sauce in with the veggies.

Made this today and the whole family enjoyed it. I used bone-in thighs and didn't have time to marinate so I brushed the sauced over the chicken, then seared it in a cast iron skillet for about 3-4 mins on each side. Then I placed the chicken in a 13x9 inch dish, brushed on a little more sauce then baked for about 35 minutes. I wasn't able to find sesame oil so I subbed olive oil. I also used a cornstarch slurry to thicken up the remaining sauce.

Made this last night and it was absolutely terrific! I opted to cut the sesame oil in half from the marinade because I know it can be very strong. I added one tablespoon of 'coarse ground black pepper' which I love from a different recipe. It definitely added some additional heat which I love. I also added a quarter cup of sliced 'scallion whites' to the marinade. And I extended the cooking time from 30 to 40 minutes which made the thighs super soft and tender. Served with steamed broccoli and carrots, and steamed jasmine rice. Out-of-the-park home run! Will definitely make this again and again! PS: Next time I may add a tablespoon of of grated fresh ginger. :)

Surprisingly very bland. I marinated chicken thighs (bone and skin on) overnight too. Recipe calls for way too much sesame oil, I highly recommend cutting that in half. I also added fresh grated ginger. I probably would add more soy sauce and reduce the rice vinegar too but we probably won't use this recipe again.

This was an amazing dish. I opted for wings over thighs this time and let them marinate 24 hours. As I gathered the ingredients I could not resist adding 2 tbsp of grated ginger and I'm so glad I did. After 10 minutes in the air fryer the result was pure perfection. Sticky, messy finger food.

Asian Glazed Chicken Thighs by Essanaye. I marinated, but didn't follow baking directions. 3T cornstarch is the right amount to thicken the sauce - for about 2# 1/4c honey, 1/3c soy, 1/2c vinegar, 3T chile garlic sauce, 2T sesame oil. I only decreased honey by 1T & it maybeee could use more. Bake 1c rice with this.

I loved this. I confess I had to use maple syrup simply because I didn't have honey on hand. I marinated the chicken and then decided to grill it on my stovetop grill pan rather than doing it in the oven. I boiled the marinade to use for serving, sliced the chicken after resting and poured the glaze over. Garnished with cilantro and scallions. Will make on repeat!
This was easy and good. I didn't use the chili paste.
easy and delicious
easy, delicious and a family favorite!

My whole family loved it! And I have to admit that I accidentally didn’t follow the directions correctly. I marinated the chicken in all of the marinade so I didn’t have any to make the sauce. Even so it was delicious! I can only imagine how flavorful it would have been if I bothered to read the instructions lol.I will definitely be making this again! Thanks for the recipe.
I’ve made this recipe several times. First time I made it I poured all the marinade into the chicken, unintentionally. I used hoisin sauce to baste it and did it on the grill. So yummy!!!! 😋😋😋🤤
Grilled marinated chicken thighs and they were delicious. Will try oven baked next time
Excellent and super easy. I only used two tablespoons of garlic chili sauce. Might add ginger and cilantro next time
Family loves this one and we serve it about every two weeks. I've replaced the honey with hot honey to give it a bit more heat.
My husband and I loved the flavor. I will definitely be making it again.
